agent_guidance_disclaimer: DIAGNOSTIC SUITE ONLY — USE ENGINEERING JUDGMENT: All 10 scenarios always run to provide complete physical telemetry, but not every test applies to every object shape. For example: spheres/cylinders SHOULD roll at <5 deg on the tilt table and should NOT self-stack; solid blocks have no cavity to probe; rigid objects have 0 joints; tall goblets should tip before sliding. Treat 'CHECK' badges as diagnostic clues to evaluate in context, not blind pass/fail rules.

warnings: Root <body> name 'block' does not match modelname 'good_block'.

1_six_pose_drop_and_hover.agent_note: Positive upright_vis_hover_mm > 2mm means collision hulls protrude below the visual mesh (tabletop hover); negative < -2mm means visual mesh sinks into the floor.

2_tilt_table_sweep.agent_note: Diagnostic telemetry: Flat-bottomed objects typically slip at arctan(mu) ~ 25-42 deg; tall objects tip at arctan(base_half_width / com_height); spheres/cylinders roll immediately (<5 deg). Compare tip angle against com_height_pct_of_z_span (50.0%) and z_band_mass_density to verify CoM height is physically realistic (e.g. weighted pot base vs airy upper foliage).

3_roll_and_isotropy.agent_note: Diagnostic telemetry: Inspect z_band_mass_density, com_height_pct_of_z_span, and hull_density_cv together. Homogeneous single-material objects should have uniform density across hulls (hull_density_cv ~ 0), whereas composite / multi-material objects (e.g., solid pot base + airy foliage canopy, or metal tool head + handle) SHOULD have different densities per material region (hull_density_cv > 0.15 is physically expected and does NOT trigger any warning).

4_three_axis_ray_and_cavity_probe.agent_note: Diagnostic telemetry: Inspect the ray-hit visualization, dropped marble resting positions, plugged_ray_count_of_400, and plugged_through_holes_by_axis in context. Open containers (bowls, mugs), neck undercuts, and functional handle/clip loops should be unobstructed so marbles enter the cavity and loop rays pass through; foliage canopies, bristles, and fine decorative crevices SHOULD be wrapped in smooth envelope hulls.

5_com_aligned_grasp_lift_shake.agent_note: Diagnostic telemetry: Gripper pads auto-scale to object size & CoM height. Inspect grasp_retained, lift_slip_mm, and shake_slip_mm in context.

6_articulation_sweep_and_polarity.agent_note: If articulated joints exist, check closes_at_limit vs opens_at_limit polarity, verify minimal degrees of freedom (no uncoupled floppy pivot links), verify internal_contacts_at_limits do not block motion, and verify position-holding joints (height slides, friction hinges) satisfy frictionloss > gravity_load_at_mid so they do not sag under gravity.

7_cliff_ledge_overhang_slide.agent_note: Diagnostic telemetry: Flat-bottomed box-like objects tip near ~50% overhang; chamfered-base bottles may hook the pusher rim, and spheres/cylinders roll off early (~10%). Check com_local_m directly for horizontal CoM symmetry.

8_twin_self_stack_and_nudge.agent_note: Flat-topped objects (boxes, closed lunchboxes, coasters, books) should stack stably; curved/spherical/open-topped objects naturally roll or nest off each other.

9_pendulum_impact_and_sites.agent_note: Striker mass scales with object hull volume (0.5 g/cm3 * V_hull) and strike speed scales with sqrt(g * L), exposing 10x mass/density outliers. Also verifies <site> groups (group=4) and Z-heights.

10_high_speed_thin_slab_drop.agent_note: Drops from 6x object max_dim onto a thin slab (20% of object min_dim) to test scale-invariant tunneling, contact penetration, and bounce ratio.
